questions.stem: Why are alkenes more reactive than alkanes?

options.text: Their C=C double bond is a region of high electron density that attracts electrophiles

questions.explanation: The C=C double bond in alkenes is a region of high electron density, which attracts electrophiles (electron-seeking species). The pi bond within the double bond is relatively weak and can break to allow addition reactions, making alkenes much more reactive than alkanes.
